doc.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The bandstand as an altar and the eternal spirit
summary: He calls the bandstand a place of prayer and says the spirit, unlike the soul, is eternal.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Yeah. That’s what you want. Why, actually, all of them did. It became a religious situation. When you get up on the altar, that’s where the – where you ask the spirit. It’s like Delano Dean, my friend Delano Dean. He had the club called Both/And, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, Both/And, the spirit. Devil can take your soul, but he can’t take your spirit. The spirit last forever. You can sell your soul to the Devil,

but he can’t mess with your spirit. Your spirit is eternal. Just to show that, as long as you can say someone’s name, you can – that spirit comes out, and you remember what they were like. That’s their spirit. The soul can – you say, okay, I’ll give this up if I can get this, and that – the soul only lasts, but the spirit is eternal. So it’s important to realize, as you’re playing music, that you want people to remember your spirit, your love of life, your thoughtfulness, your peace of mind, where you stand, God, your family, and your children, your friends around you. One more note: no matter what you do, I’ll always love you. I stand behind you. I’m always there for you. Your spirit, the look in your eye, the understanding that as you walk down life’s paths, you’re on the edge. You can fall over on the side anytime. The roads are not safe.
